newsitem.title: USA: ENOVA,PACENT TO BUY AIG TRADING CORP.
newsitem.headline: ENOVA,PACENT TO BUY AIG TRADING CORP.

text.p: Enova Corp and Pacific Enterprises on Thursday announced they would pay $190 million to acquire AIG Trading Corp in a move that weds the giant California power suppliers to an energy trading firm.
The acquisition comes as the U.S. utiilty industry is being deregulated, heightening competition for power customers.
In June, Enova and Pacific Enterprises (PE) won preliminary approval from the government to merge in a $2.5 billion deal creating the nation's largest U.S. utility in terms of customers.
"This transaction establishes the wholesale commodity trading business necessary to support our retail marketing," said Stephen Baum, president and chief executive officer of Enova Corp.
"Now we will have a full portfolio of energy services for our customers," he said.
PE is the parent company of Southern California Gas Co (SoCal Gas), and Enova's main subsidiary is San Diego Gas & Electric Co.
The merger gives Connecticut-based AIG Trading Corp access to massive generation and transmission resources.

"Because of the dawn of deregulation...we feel this company will grow faster...marrying a trade and operating sensibility," said Robert Rubin, executive vice president of AIG Trading Group, which is selling off the energy trading and marketing company.
The utiltities will acquire all of the outstanding common stock of AIG Trading Corp, one of the nations's leading natural gas and power marketers.
Each company is funding half of the acquisition, which is expected to be accounted for as a purchase.
The acquisition will require approval from the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC), and is expected to be completed before the end of this year.
